replacements.text: The routing table in the delegation skill is meant to be the only inventory of model ids. Nothing enforced that. A new test suite now reads the Markdown files under `src/`, except those under an `evals` or `node_modules` directory. The suite fails `make ci` on a model id the table does not list. Anthropic aliases such as `sonnet` are not caught.
The lint rejects a word that is not a model id. That rejection blocks every pull request.
The patterns are case-sensitive. The real tree of 94 files lints clean.
Nothing ships from the test file. Therefore, delete it.
An unlisted id appended to a skill made `make content-tests` exit 2. That run named the line.
Each vendor naming scheme has one case-sensitive pattern. Therefore, a family name in prose is not an id.
The lint allows two tables in the routing file. Therefore, the routing file's Providers table became a list.
The spec defines ids by vendor naming scheme. An alias is not one.
A table row elsewhere that names a listed id fails. The same id in prose passes.

A pytest suite beside the delegation skill reads every Markdown file under src/, except those under an evals or node_modules directory. It fails on a model id the routing table does not list and on a table row elsewhere that names one. It also fails on a routing table that has changed shape. The lint's limit of two tables in the routing file causes the Providers table to become a list.

make ci exits 0 at the head. 20 content suites pass. All 34 cases fail against a stub lint. Every case passes at the head. One unlisted id appended to a skill made the gate exit 2. That run named the line. Anthropic aliases are not caught. No review round ran.
An absent or empty routing table fails with its name.

questions.question: Please add a separate Heads-up row for the caveat that Anthropic aliases such as `sonnet` are not caught; the existing Heads-up row covers only the missing review round.
What does PEP 723 mean, and what is the tier grid? The record does not supply meanings for their first-use explanations.
